title: Scheme-theoretic module support eventually becomes proper over a stage
statement: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme], algebraic spaces and their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use quasi-coherent modules [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] and canonical tensor pullback [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme, and quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests. An affine morphism is representable and has affine source after pullback to any affine scheme test. A morphism is of finite presentation if it is quasi-compact, quasi-separated, and locally of finite presentation on etale scheme charts; local finite presentation means chart ring maps have finitely many generators and relations. A module is finitely presented if etale locally it has an exact presentation $\mathcal O^m\to\mathcal O^n\to M\to0$ with $m,n$ finite. Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set, $(T_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of affine schemes with affine transitions and limit $T$, and $i_0\in I$. Let $f_{i_0}:X_{i_0}\to T_{i_0}$ be a finitely presented algebraic space. For $i\ge i_0$ put $X_i=X_{i_0}\times_{T_{i_0}}T_i$, $f_i:X_i\to T_i$, and put $X=X_{i_0}\times_{T_{i_0}}T$, $f:X\to T$. Let $M_{i_0}$ be a quasi-coherent finitely presented module on $X_{i_0}$, with ordinary tensor pullbacks $M_i$ on $X_i$ and $M$ on $X$. For any such module $N$, its scheme-theoretic support is the closed subspace defined by the quasi-coherent annihilator ideal of functions killing all local sections. Proper means separated, of finite type and universally closed [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. If the scheme-theoretic support of $M$ is proper over $T$, then for some $j\ge i_0$ the scheme-theoretic support of $M_j$ is proper over $T_j$. No flatness of any module or transition map is assumed.

source.place: Tag 08K2 (lemma-eventually-proper-support), in Situation 084W (situation-descent-property), specialized to a finitely presented space and finitely presented module over affine bases.

proof.text: Put $A_0=\operatorname{Ann}(M_{i_0})$ and let $W_{i_0}\hookrightarrow X_{i_0}$ be its closed subspace, supplied by [lem-sfb-space-module-proper-carrier-support]. Finite presentation gives finite generation. On an affine etale chart with module $N$ generated by $n_1,\ldots,n_r$, $N_{\mathfrak p}=0$ iff each generator is killed by an element outside $\mathfrak p$; multiplying these finitely many elements gives one element of $\operatorname{Ann}(N)$ outside $\mathfrak p$. Thus the annihilator closed locus is exactly the module support. On etale charts this identifies $|W_{i_0}|$ with $\operatorname{Supp}(M_{i_0})$ (the chart support identification is [lem-sfb-space-etale-chart-support]). The affine base is qcqs: it is its own affine atlas and its diagonal is closed on affine tests. Since $f_{i_0}$ is quasi-compact, $X_{i_0}$ is quasi-compact; since it is quasi-separated, [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-source-products] gives quasi-separatedness of $X_{i_0}$. Restricting a finite affine etale atlas to a closed subspace gives a finite affine atlas of $W_{i_0}$; its relation is closed in the qc relation for $X_{i_0}$, hence qc. Thus $W_{i_0}$ is qcqs. Its chart rings are quotients of finite type chart algebras over $T_{i_0}$, hence still finite type. In particular $W_{i_0}\to T_{i_0}$ is locally finite type; no finite generation of $A_0$ is asserted.

source.place: Tag 08K2 (lemma-eventually-proper-support), proof; spaces-morphisms.tex Tags 07U0, 07TZ and 03MB; spaces-more-morphisms.tex Tag 09ZY.

proof.text: For every stage, and also at the limit, write $p:X'\to X_{i_0}$, $N=p^*M_{i_0}$ and $W'=W_{i_0}\times_{X_{i_0}}X'$. By [lem-sfb-space-closed-ideal-correspondence], the ideal of $W'$ is $A'=\operatorname{im}(p^*A_0\to\mathcal O_{X'})$. It annihilates $N$: locally $a(b\otimes m)=b\otimes(am)=0$ for $a\in A_0$. Therefore $A'\subseteq\operatorname{Ann}(N)$, giving a closed immersion $Z_N\hookrightarrow W'$. Here $Z_N$ exists by [lem-sfb-space-module-proper-carrier-support], since pullback is finite type quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-space-finite-type-support-pullback]. That same lemma gives $\operatorname{Supp}(N)=|p|^{-1}\operatorname{Supp}(M_{i_0})$. The underlying locus of $W'$ is $|p|^{-1}|W_{i_0}|$: on a geometric point the extended ideal vanishes precisely when the original ideal vanishes. By step 1, applied also to $N$ on charts, $|Z_N|=\operatorname{Supp}(N)$. Consequently $Z_N\hookrightarrow W'$ is a thickening, a closed immersion inducing a homeomorphism. This asserts no equality of annihilator ideals under non-flat pullback.

source.place: Tag 08K2 (lemma-eventually-proper-support), proof; spaces-morphisms.tex Tags 07U0, 07TZ and 03MB; spaces-more-morphisms.tex Tag 09ZY.

proof.text: At the limit put $W=W_{i_0}\times_{T_{i_0}}T$ and $Z=Z_M$. The structure maps form a morphism of thickenings $(Z\subset W)\to(T\subset T)$ by step 2. Since $Z\to T$ is proper by hypothesis, [lem-sfb-space-thickening-topological-properties] implies that $W\to T$ is separated, quasi-compact and universally closed. It is locally finite type: in a finite type chart algebra, extending scalars preserves its finite list of generators, and quotienting preserves finite generation as an algebra. These are exactly the charts obtained by base change from step 1. Hence $W\to T$ is proper.

source.place: Tag 08K2 (lemma-eventually-proper-support), proof; spaces-morphisms.tex Tags 07U0, 07TZ and 03MB; spaces-more-morphisms.tex Tag 09ZY.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-finite-type-eventually-proper] to $W_{i_0}\to T_{i_0}$ and the given affine-base inverse system. The indexing set is small, nonempty and directed; step 1 proves the required qcqs and local finite type hypotheses for $W_{i_0}$; step 3 proves properness at the limit. Obtain $j\ge i_0$ with $W_j\to T_j$ proper. The fibre product $W_j=W_{i_0}\times_{T_{i_0}}T_j$ is also $W_{i_0}\times_{X_{i_0}}X_j$: a section on either side is a section of $W_{i_0}$ and one of $T_j$ with equal images in $T_{i_0}$.

source.place: Tag 08K2 (lemma-eventually-proper-support), proof; spaces-morphisms.tex Tags 07U0, 07TZ and 03MB; spaces-more-morphisms.tex Tag 09ZY.

proof.text: At stage $j$, step 2 supplies a closed immersion $Z_{M_j}\hookrightarrow W_j$. It is proper by [lem-sfb-space-closed-subspace-proper]. Compose it with the proper map $W_j\to T_j$ of step 4 and use [lem-sfb-space-proper-composition]. The result is precisely that the scheme-theoretic support of $M_j$ is proper over $T_j$, as required.
